messages:
incident-bot: URGENT: KV-cache memory spike on prod-cluster-a. Continuous-batching queue depth rising, paging to NVMe started, multiple shard NCCL stalls detected. Auto-mitigation: trace collection started, paging throttle NOT applied. Alert severity: P1. @oncall please ack. :fire:

eli_ml: Acked. I'm looking. Initial glance: backend metrics show continuous_batcher token rate jumped ~3x at 15:12 UTC, KV cache resident set went from 60% -> 210% of configured slab. Paging throughput saturated NVMe on nodes gpux-0..3.

sam_infra: Seeing NCCL errors on tp-shard-2 and tp-shard-3: "NCCL WARN Call to cuCommInitRank failed" followed by long stalls in all-reduce. Logs attached to incident storage.

maya_sre: Confirmed customer-facing errors for several requests (504s) around 15:14-15:21 UTC. Error rate peaked ~8% for model /gptx-6b-optimized; rolling fallback to cpu-models triggered for some tenants.

eli_ml: Quick mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching on prod cluster-a (hotfix config flip), 2) set kv-cache eviction threshold to 65% and enable aggressive prefix evict, 3) rebalance KV shard partitioning for TP group to avoid uneven hot shard. Who can cut the config hotpatch?

sam_infra: I can cut the config. Preparing a single-line hotpatch to disable continuous batching and cap batch size. Applying to canary nodes first.

jordan_support: Noted increased support load. Customer-facing status page updated with "degraded" and estimated ETA 30m. Notifying top 10 customers currently impacted.

eli_ml: Hotpatch snippet (applied via rollout tool):

```json
{
  "continuous_batching": false,
  "batch_config": {
    "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
    "max_batch_items": 8,
    "batch_timeout_ms": 20
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "eviction_threshold_percent": 65,
    "prefix_eviction": "aggressive"
  }
}
```

sam_infra: Pushing to canary: `rollout apply --cluster prod-cluster-a --selector canary=true --file hotfix.json`

sam_infra: Canary nodes passed initial health checks (3/3). Rolling to remaining nodes now.

ana_reliability: (reaction) :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: oncall swap requested: eli_ml -> maya_sre at 15:28 UTC.

maya_sre: Taking over incident. Observing KV resident set dropping after eviction enabled. Paging rate dropping ~60% within 5 minutes. NCCL stalls persist but fewer new occurrences. Need to address uneven TP partitioning that caused hotspot on shards 2/3.

carlos_prod: Found root cause indicator: a recent rollout of the dynamic-kv-sharder introduced non-deterministic hashing for long-prefix keys causing skew. Repro snippet in staging: some prefixes mapped 60% of keys to tp-shard-2.

eli_ml: Thanks, Carlos. That explains blowup: hot prefixes caused one shard to accumulate enormous KV state, triggering continuous-batching to form very large batches and blow past slab size. Combined with NCCL all-reduce pressure, stalls happened.

sam_infra: For live mitigation I pushed a temporary denylist for the problematic prefix ranges on prod (shard-slicer -> denylist add). This forces even hashing fallback for those prefixes. Deployed at 15:36 UTC.

maya_sre: After denylist + eviction + disabling continuous-batching: paging is under control, 504s down to baseline within 12 minutes. Rolling restart not required.

jordan_support: Update to customers: we’ve applied a mitigation and are seeing recovery; some in-flight requests may have been retried. ETA for full root cause patch 24 hours.

eli_ml: Next steps assigned: 1) patch dynamic-kv-sharder hashing determinism + add unit tests for prefix distribution -> assignee carlos_prod, due 12 hours; 2) add circuit-breaker in continuous-batcher to cap batch token growth -> assignee eli_ml, due 8 hours; 3) postmortem & customer impact summary -> assignee jordan_support, due EOD.

maya_sre: One remaining concern: NCCL stall traces show occasionally stale communicator handles when a GPU is hit with extreme memory pressure. We'll add additional guards: reduce NCCL timeout and add retry/backoff around collectives. Sam to schedule rolling node-level nv_peer_mem restart in low-traffic window.

sam_infra: Will schedule drainer window and coordinate with oncall for rolling reboots. Also creating a metric alert for kv-cache per-shard imbalance (ratio of max_shard_bytes / median_shard_bytes > 2).

eli_ml: Marking incident as mitigated at 15:44 UTC. Impact: intermittent 504s for ~10 minutes, elevated token cost due to paging during window. Customers impacted: 12 tenants saw degraded latency, 3 had transient timeouts. No data loss.

ana_reliability: Please make sure the new alert and unit tests land before rolling dynamic-kv-sharder to other regions.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status -> MITIGATED. Please file postmortem.

jordan_support: Filing customer impact doc and will post summary in #customer-status.

eli_ml: Thanks team. Will open PR for continuous-batcher circuit-breaker now.

maya_sre: Adding post-incident checklist items to runbook: - add per-prefix hot-key detector, - enforce shard-symmetry checks during sharder rollout, - add emergency disable flag for continuous-batching.

carlos_prod: Pushing deterministic hashing patch to staging for validation.

eli_ml: Closing thread for now. Follow-ups tracked in the incident tracker: INC-2254326789.

(added: logs archived to s3://incidents/2254326789/trace.tar.gz, and link to rollback-safe hotfix: https://rollouts.internal/release/2254326789)
